defects.observed: Planet labels are not attached to their planets. Each label lives in a separate <g class="counter-N"> that is animated with a rotate(0deg)->rotate(-360deg) keyframe about the sun's transform-origin (640px 340px), i.e. the labels revolve BACKWARDS around the sun while the planets revolve forwards. In t2.png the 'Mars' label sits at the top of the outer orbit (~655,197) while the red Mars planet is at the bottom (~676,649) — 180 degrees apart; 'Earth' is upper-left (~520,308) while the blue Earth planet is lower-left (~543,554); 'Mercury' (~580,500) is opposite the grey Mercury planet (~568,360). In t5.png the labels have drifted to yet other separations (Earth label bottom-right at ~714,570 vs Earth planet top at ~692,271). Only in t0.png are they roughly in the same quadrant.
defects.required: Prompt requires labelled planets; rubric item 6 requires labels attached to the right shapes. Labels must travel with their planet at the same angular rate and phase.

defects.observed: Label text is rotated and frequently upside-down/mirrored, making it illegible. The comment claims 'Counter-rotate labels so they stay upright and readable', but the -360deg rotation is applied to the group containing the <text>, so the glyphs rotate with it and nothing cancels the glyph rotation. t2.png shows 'Earth' and 'Mercury' rendered upside-down; t5.png shows 'Mars' upside-down and 'Mercury' tilted ~60 degrees; even t0.png shows all three labels skewed off horizontal.
defects.required: Rubric item 4: text must be legible. Labels must remain upright at all times.

defects.observed: Body text is well below presentation size: .legend-text (planet/Sun labels) is 15px and .orbit-caption (the 'Mercury: 4s / orbit' block) is 13px in a 1280x720 viewBox that renders 1:1. The caption lines are rendered in low-contrast #8b93b0 on a dark navy field.
defects.required: Rubric item 4: body text >= ~20px equivalent with sufficient contrast.

defects.observed: The three period captions (y=470/500/530) are placed inside the orbit field, on top of the dashed orbit paths, and are crossed by moving elements: Mercury's r=110 orbit passes through y=450 directly above the first caption (planet body spans y 438-462 vs caption top ~458), and the free-roaming labels pass through the caption block — in t5.png the 'Earth' label (~714,570) nearly collides with the 'Mars: 11s / orbit' caption, and in t2.png the 'Mercury' label (~580,500) sits immediately left of the caption stack.
defects.required: Rubric item 3: no overlapping elements; item 4: no text on top of busy graphics.

defects.observed: The solar system is drawn centered at SVG (640,340) but the composition sits low and left-of-center in the frame with large empty regions at left and right, and the 'Sun' label (y=410) floats inside the sun's glow halo rather than clear of it.
defects.required: Rubric item 2: layout should read as a deliberate, balanced arrangement.

summary: Core mechanics are present and animating correctly — sun at center, three planets on three visible dashed orbit circles, distinct 4s/7s/11s linear infinite periods, positions clearly differ across t0/t2/t5, planets measure on their orbit radii, no console errors and no overflow (1280x720). But the labelling is fundamentally broken: each label group is animated with a -360deg rotation about the sun instead of riding with its planet, so the labels orbit backwards, separate from (and at t2 sit exactly opposite) the planets they name, and the glyphs render rotated and upside-down despite a comment claiming counter-rotation. Compounded by sub-20px low-contrast caption text overlapping the orbit field.
